name: Frankland Reaction
productName: Diethylzinc (organozinc); alkane R-R with excess halide/heat
summary: Alkyl iodides react with zinc to give dialkylzinc compounds, the first organometallics discovered; with heating or excess halide they can give alkanes R-R (Wurtz-like).
mechanism: Zinc inserts into the C-I bond to give RZnI, which disproportionates to R2Zn and ZnI2. R2Zn is a weak carbanion source and can couple with R-X to give R-R.
keyPoints: Zn is less reactive than Mg: R2Zn is less basic than Grignard reagents
Dry conditions needed as R2Zn is spontaneously flammable in air and destroyed by water
whenUsed: Historic route to organometallics; precursor of Reformatsky-type reagents

examples.eq: 2 C2H5I + 2 Zn ->[\text{dry ether}][\Delta] C2H5ZnI + ZnI2 + C4H10
examples.note: Zinc-mediated coupling gives butane in part

jeeTips: Compare with Wurtz (Na, gives only R-R) and Corey-House. Dialkylzinc reacts with acid chlorides to give ketones. Do not confuse with Reformatsky (alpha-bromo ester + Zn).

name: Isomerisation of Alkanes
summary: Straight-chain alkanes rearrange to branched isomers in presence of anhydrous AlCl3 and HCl; branched alkanes have higher octane number.
mechanism: AlCl3/HCl generates a carbocation by hydride abstraction. The carbocation undergoes 1,2-hydride and 1,2-methyl shifts to a more stable branched cation, which abstracts hydride from another alkane to give the isomer (chain process).
keyPoints: Proceeds through carbocation intermediates via H- and CH3- shifts
Equilibrium favours more branched/stable isomer at low temperature
whenUsed: Petroleum refining to raise octane rating; industrial alkylation feed
jeeTips: Reagent is anhydrous AlCl3 with HCl, not Friedel-Crafts. Industrial refinery version uses Pt/Al2O3 (reforming). Expect 'which alkane isomerises' - n-alkane gives its branched isomer.

name: Aromatisation of n-Hexane
summary: Alkanes with six or more carbons undergo dehydrogenation and cyclisation over metal oxide catalyst at high temperature and pressure to give arenes.
mechanism: Adsorbed hexane is dehydrogenated and ring-closes (dehydrocyclisation) to cyclohexane, which is further dehydrogenated to benzene with loss of hydrogen.
keyPoints: n-Hexane gives benzene; n-heptane gives toluene; n-octane gives xylenes
Also called hydroforming; catalysts Cr2O3, V2O5, Mo2O3 on alumina
whenUsed: Industrial source of benzene, toluene, xylenes from petroleum
jeeTips: Four H2 molecules are lost per ring formed (loss of 4 H2 for hexane: C6H14 to C6H6). Cr2O3-Al2O3 at 773 K is the key pairing to remember.

name: Fischer Indole Synthesis
summary: An aryl hydrazone of an aldehyde or ketone bearing alpha-H cyclises under acid to an indole with loss of NH3.
mechanism: Hydrazone tautomerises to an ene-hydrazine, which undergoes [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement to give a C-C bond. Rearomatisation, cyclisation to an aminal and loss of NH3 give the indole.
keyPoints: Needs alpha-CH2 on the carbonyl partner
Acetaldehyde does not work, so indole itself is made from pyruvic acid then decarboxylation
N from the aryl N-N is lost as NH3 (the NH attached to the ring's ortho carbon carries over)
whenUsed: Synthesis of indoles, tryptamines, triptan drugs
jeeTips: Key step is [3,3] shift; ammonia is lost. Count ring atoms: indole = benzene fused with pyrrole.

name: Gomberg-Bachmann Reaction
summary: Aryl diazonium salt couples with an arene in presence of base to form a biaryl through aryl radicals.
mechanism: Base converts the diazonium salt to a diazoanhydride, which homolyses to aryl radical + N2. The aryl radical adds to the arene, and loss of H gives biaryl.
keyPoints: Radical mechanism; mixtures of o-, m-, p- isomers from substituted arenes
Yields low (below 40%) due to side reactions

examples.eq: C6H5N2+ Cl- + C6H6 ->[NaOH] C6H5-C6H5 + N2 + NaCl + H2O

jeeTips: Compare with Ullmann (Cu, ArI), Fittig (Na, ArX) and Wurtz-Fittig. Azo coupling does not occur here because base conditions generate radicals, not ArN2+ electrophile with activated arenes.

name: Sharpless Asymmetric Epoxidation
summary: Allylic alcohols are converted to 2,3-epoxy alcohols with high enantioselectivity using titanium tetraisopropoxide, a chiral tartrate and tert-butyl hydroperoxide.
mechanism: The allylic alcohol, tartrate and TBHP bind to titanium in a chiral complex; peroxide oxygen is delivered to one face of the C=C, giving the epoxide with predictable stereochemistry.
keyPoints: Works only on allylic alcohols (OH needed for Ti binding)
Choice of (+)-DET or (-)-DET fixes which face is epoxidised
Syn-addition of O, retains alkene geometry
whenUsed: Asymmetric synthesis of chiral building blocks; Nobel 2001 (Sharpless)
jeeTips: Differs from Prilezhaev (achiral, any alkene, peracid). Chirality induced by tartrate, oxidant is TBHP, not H2O2.

name: Clauson-Kaas Pyrrole Synthesis
summary: A primary amine condenses with 2,5-dimethoxytetrahydrofuran in acid to give an N-substituted pyrrole.
mechanism: Acid hydrolyses the acetal to succinaldehyde (butane-1,4-dial equivalent). The amine condenses twice with the two aldehyde groups, cyclisation and loss of water gives the aromatic pyrrole.
keyPoints: The dialdehyde equivalent is cyclic acetal; amine must be primary
Related to Paal-Knorr (1,4-dicarbonyl + amine gives pyrrole)
jeeTips: Remember pyrrole is aromatic (6 pi e-, N lone pair in sextet). Amine nitrogen becomes ring nitrogen.

name: Vilsmeier-Haack Reaction
summary: Electron-rich arenes are formylated by the chloroiminium (Vilsmeier) reagent from DMF and POCl3, followed by hydrolysis.
mechanism: DMF + POCl3 gives chloroiminium ion [Me2N=CHCl]+. This weak electrophile attacks the electron-rich ring (SEAr); the resulting iminium salt is hydrolysed to the aldehyde.
keyPoints: Only activated arenes (phenols, anilines, pyrroles, furans) react
Para product favoured for anilines
whenUsed: Alternative to Gattermann-Koch for activated rings
jeeTips: Not applicable for benzene or deactivated rings. Formyl C comes from DMF. Compare Gattermann-Koch (CO/HCl, AlCl3) and Reimer-Tiemann.

name: Willgerodt-Kindler Reaction
summary: Aryl alkyl ketones are converted to the terminal thioamide (or amide) of the same carbon number, by heating with sulphur and an amine; hydrolysis gives a carboxylic acid.
mechanism: Ketone forms an enamine with amine, which reacts with sulphur to give a thioamide; the carbonyl effectively migrates along the chain to the terminal position through repeated enamine/thioketone shifts.
keyPoints: Carbonyl oxygen moves to terminal carbon without changing carbon count
Willgerodt: (NH4)2Sx; Kindler: S8 + amine
whenUsed: Chain-end functionalisation of aryl alkyl ketones
jeeTips: Product acid has same carbon count as ketone. Acetophenone gives phenylacetic acid, not benzoic acid.

name: Stobbe Condensation
summary: Diethyl succinate condenses with aldehydes or ketones in presence of a strong base to give alkylidene succinic acid half-esters.
mechanism: Enolate of succinate adds to carbonyl (aldol); the alkoxide attacks the neighbouring ester to form a gamma-lactone intermediate, which opens by E1cB to the unsaturated acid-ester.
keyPoints: Only one ester group is hydrolysed (half-ester)
Succinic ester is essential; lactone intermediate
Uses 1 mol base, not catalytic
whenUsed: Synthesis of unsaturated acids, extension of carbon chain
jeeTips: Remember product is half-ester, free COOH on the CH2 side. Compare with Perkin and Knoevenagel (different active methylene).

name: Pechmann Condensation
summary: A phenol condenses with a beta-keto ester in presence of acid to give a coumarin (benzopyran-2-one).
mechanism: Transesterification of phenol OH with the ester, then intramolecular electrophilic attack (hydroxyalkylation) of the ketone on the ortho position of the ring, and dehydration give the coumarin.
keyPoints: Activated phenols (resorcinol, phloroglucinol) react easily
Acid catalyst: H2SO4, AlCl3, ion exchange
Beta-keto ester supplies C2-C4 of the coumarin
jeeTips: Compare with Perkin (salicylaldehyde + Ac2O gives coumarin). Two different routes to coumarin: Perkin and Pechmann.

name: Bouveault-Blanc Reduction
summary: Esters are reduced to primary alcohols by sodium metal in absolute ethanol, without affecting isolated C=C bonds.
mechanism: Sodium transfers electrons to the ester carbonyl, giving a radical anion; protonation by ethanol and repetition give an aldehyde that is reduced further to the primary alcohol.
keyPoints: Does not reduce isolated C=C
Cheaper alternative to LiAlH4
Ester gives two alcohols: one from acid part and the one from alkoxy part
whenUsed: Old industrial route to fatty alcohols
jeeTips: Compare LiAlH4 (reduces C=C only when conjugated slightly) and Birch. Reducing agent is Na/EtOH; acyloin condensation uses Na in aprotic solvent.

name: Meerwein Arylation
summary: An aryl diazonium salt adds an aryl radical across an activated alkene (acrylate, acrylonitrile, styrene) under copper catalysis, giving chloroarylalkane or, after loss of HCl, the arylalkene.
mechanism: Cu(I) reduces ArN2+ to Ar radical + N2. The aryl radical adds to the alkene to form a stabilised radical, which abstracts Cl from CuCl2 (or loses H) to give the product.
keyPoints: Radical addition; alkene needs electron-withdrawing group or conjugation
Elimination of HCl can follow, giving cinnamate
Ar adds to the CH2 end
jeeTips: Compare with Sandmeyer (ArN2+ to ArX) and Gomberg-Bachmann (arene partner). Meerwein = alkene partner.

name: Simmons-Smith Reaction
summary: Alkenes react with diiodomethane and zinc-copper couple to give cyclopropanes stereospecifically through a zinc carbenoid.
mechanism: Zn(Cu) inserts into CH2I2 to give ICH2ZnI, a carbenoid. It transfers CH2 to the alkene in a concerted syn manner via a three-centre transition state.
keyPoints: Stereospecific syn addition: cis alkene gives cis-disubstituted cyclopropane
Free carbene is not involved (carbenoid)
Allylic OH directs addition to the same face
jeeTips: Distinguish from dichlorocarbene addition (gives gem-dihalo ring). Stereospecific syn addition; the reagent is a carbenoid not free :CH2.

name: Dichlorocarbene Addition (alpha-Elimination of CHCl3)
summary: Strong base abstracts H from chloroform, and the CCl3- anion loses Cl- (alpha-elimination) giving electrophilic singlet :CCl2, which adds to C=C to give gem-dichlorocyclopropanes.
mechanism: Step 1: CHCl3 + OH- -> CCl3- + H2O. Step 2: CCl3- -> :CCl2 + Cl-. Step 3: concerted stereospecific syn addition of :CCl2 to alkene.
keyPoints: Alpha-elimination: both H and Cl from the same carbon
Dichlorocarbene is electrophilic (six electrons on C)
Also the electrophile in Reimer-Tiemann and the carbylamine reaction
jeeTips: Same :CCl2 explains Reimer-Tiemann (phenol to salicylaldehyde) and carbylamine (RNH2 to RNC). Trap: 3-membered ring formed.

name: Strecker Amino Acid Synthesis
summary: An aldehyde with ammonia and cyanide gives an alpha-aminonitrile, hydrolysed to a racemic alpha-amino acid.
mechanism: Aldehyde + NH3 forms an imine/iminium; cyanide adds to give alpha-aminonitrile. Acid hydrolysis of the CN group gives the carboxylic acid.
keyPoints: Product has one more carbon than the aldehyde
Racemic mixture of amino acid
Ketones give alpha,alpha-disubstituted amino acids
jeeTips: Aldehyde C becomes alpha-carbon. HCHO gives glycine (optically inactive), others racemic. Compare Gabriel and Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky amination for amino acids.

name: Kiliani-Fischer Synthesis
reagents: HCN; then H2O, then H2 / Pd-BaSO4
productName: Aldose with one more carbon (C2 epimers)
summary: An aldose is lengthened by one carbon via cyanohydrin formation, hydrolysis to aldonic acid/lactone and reduction to the aldose.
mechanism: HCN adds to the aldehyde to give two epimeric cyanohydrins; hydrolysis gives aldonic acids (lactones); reduction (H2/Pd-BaSO4 or Na-Hg) converts them to aldoses.
keyPoints: Creates a new stereocentre at C-2: mixture of two C-2 epimers
Reverse of Ruff degradation
Pentose gives two hexoses
whenUsed: Ascent of the sugar series, synthesis of rare sugars
jeeTips: Product pair are C-2 epimers. Ascending = Kiliani-Fischer; descending = Ruff/Wohl.

name: Ruff Degradation
products: Aldose with one fewer carbon (D-Arabinose) + CO2
summary: An aldose is shortened by one carbon: oxidise to aldonic acid, then oxidative decarboxylation gives the lower aldose.
mechanism: Bromine water oxidises CHO to COOH (calcium aldonate). Fe(III)/H2O2 oxidises C-2 OH, decarboxylation gives CO2 and the lower aldose.
keyPoints: Loses the C-1 as CO2
Descending the sugar series
Reverse of Kiliani-Fischer
jeeTips: D-Glucose gives D-Arabinose (C-2 epimers D-glucose and D-mannose give same pentose). Hexose to pentose.

name: Cope Rearrangement
summary: Thermal [3,3]-sigmatropic shift of a 1,5-diene in which the central sigma bond (C3-C4) breaks and a new sigma bond (C1-C6) forms.
mechanism: Concerted pericyclic via a six-membered chair-like transition state; position of equilibrium favours the more substituted/conjugated alkene.
keyPoints: Concerted, suprafacial, intramolecular
Chair TS controls stereochemistry (meso-3,4-dimethylhexa-1,5-diene gives E,Z-octa-2,6-diene)
Reversible; goes to thermodynamically more stable diene

examples.note: Substituent ends up on a terminal-bonded alkene

jeeTips: Claisen is the oxygen analogue (allyl aryl ether). Count 1-2-3-4-5-6 atoms: bond 3-4 breaks, 1-6 forms.

name: Cope Elimination
summary: A tertiary amine oxide on heating undergoes intramolecular syn elimination (Ei) to give an alkene and a hydroxylamine.
mechanism: The N-oxide oxygen abstracts a beta-H through a five-membered cyclic TS while the C-N bond breaks, giving alkene and R2NOH.
keyPoints: Syn elimination via 5-membered cyclic TS
Amine oxide is made from tertiary amine + H2O2 or peracid
Hofmann-like orientation (less substituted alkene), no base needed
jeeTips: Syn elimination, unlike E2 (anti) of Hofmann with quaternary hydroxide. Trap: no external base.

name: Dakin Reaction
summary: ortho- or para-hydroxybenzaldehydes (or hydroxyacetophenones) are oxidised by alkaline H2O2 to dihydric phenols, with loss of formate.
mechanism: HOO- adds to the carbonyl, the aryl group migrates to O (Baeyer-Villiger-like), giving an aryl formate that hydrolyses to the phenol.
keyPoints: Needs ortho or para OH (electron donating)
m-Hydroxybenzaldehyde does not undergo it
Aryl migrates, formate lost
whenUsed: Synthesis of catechol, hydroquinone, from hydroxy-aldehydes
jeeTips: Think Baeyer-Villiger on aromatic carbonyl: aryl migrates. Product is diphenol, not carboxylic acid.

name: Prins Reaction
summary: An alkene adds to a protonated aldehyde (often formaldehyde) under acid to give 1,3-diols, 1,3-dioxanes or allylic alcohols, depending on conditions.
mechanism: Acid activates the aldehyde; the alkene pi bond attacks the carbonyl carbon to give a carbocation, which is captured by water (diol) or a second aldehyde (dioxane), or loses H+ (allylic alcohol).
keyPoints: Product depends on water, temperature, acid
Excess HCHO gives 1,3-dioxane
Carbon-carbon bond formation using alkenes and carbonyls

examples.note: Loss of H+ gives homoallylic alcohol

jeeTips: Alkene as nucleophile attacking carbonyl (reverse of usual roles). Markovnikov-type cation stability decides regiochemistry.

name: Hydrolysis of Grignard Reagent (Active-H Compounds)
summary: Grignard reagents are strong bases and react with any compound containing acidic hydrogen (water, alcohols, acids, terminal alkynes, amines) to give the alkane RH.
mechanism: The carbanion-like carbon of R-MgX abstracts a proton from the acid H-Y; R-H forms and MgXY is left.
keyPoints: RMgX + HY -> RH + Mg(X)Y
D2O gives R-D (deuterium labelling)
Zerewitinoff method counts active H by methane evolved
whenUsed: Why Grignard needs dry ether; alkane from halide; labelling
jeeTips: Frequent trap: RMgX destroyed by water, alcohol, acid, NH3, terminal alkyne. It does not react with ethers. Fate: RMgX + D2O gives R-D.

name: Pinner Reaction
summary: A nitrile reacts with an alcohol in presence of dry HCl to give an imidate hydrochloride (Pinner salt), which can be converted to esters, amidines or orthoesters.
mechanism: HCl protonates the nitrile N, making C electrophilic; the alcohol adds, and proton transfer gives the imidate salt. Water hydrolyses it to an ester + NH4Cl.
keyPoints: Strictly anhydrous: water gives ester directly
Imidate + NH3 gives amidine; + excess ROH gives orthoester
Alcohol should be unhindered
jeeTips: Compare nitrile hydrolysis (acid or base, gives acid). Pinner uses dry HCl + alcohol and stops at imidate.

name: Haworth Synthesis (Naphthalene)
summary: A second ring is built on benzene using succinic anhydride: acylation, Clemmensen reduction, cyclisation and aromatisation give naphthalene (or phenanthrene analogues).
mechanism: Step 1: Friedel-Crafts acylation gives 3-benzoylpropanoic acid. Step 2: Clemmensen gives 4-phenylbutanoic acid. Step 3: intramolecular acylation (conc. H2SO4) gives alpha-tetralone. Step 4: Clemmensen gives tetralin; Pd or Se dehydrogenates it to naphthalene.
keyPoints: Ring is fused by intramolecular Friedel-Crafts acylation
Zn-Hg/HCl converts C=O to CH2
Final dehydrogenation (Pd/Se) aromatises tetralin

examples.eq: C6H5(CH2)3COOH ->[conc. H2SO4] alpha-Tetralone ->[Zn-Hg/HCl] Tetralin ->[Pd, \Delta] C10H8 + 2 H2

jeeTips: Know sequence: acylation, Clemmensen, cyclisation, Clemmensen, dehydrogenation. Final step is dehydrogenation with Pd/Se.

name: Leuckart Reaction
summary: Aldehydes or ketones are converted to amines by heating with ammonium formate or formamide; formic acid is the reducing agent.
mechanism: The carbonyl forms an iminium ion with ammonia; formate transfers hydride to the iminium carbon, giving the N-formyl amine, which is hydrolysed to the amine.
keyPoints: Formate is the hydride source (reductive amination)
N-Formyl amine intermediate needs hydrolysis
With N-methylformamide gives N-methylamine
whenUsed: Preparing primary, secondary, tertiary amines (with HCONR2 / amine formates)

examples.eq: C6H5COCH3 + 2 HCOONH4 ->[165 C] C6H5CH(CH3)NHCHO + 2 H2O + NH3 + CO2

jeeTips: Related to reductive amination (NaBH3CN) and Eschweiler-Clarke (HCHO/HCOOH, methylation). Mention formate = hydride source.

name: Nef Reaction
summary: A primary or secondary nitroalkane is converted to an aldehyde or ketone through its nitronate salt and acid hydrolysis.
mechanism: Base gives the nitronate (aci-nitro) anion; protonation by strong acid gives the nitronic acid, which hydrolyses to the carbonyl with loss of N2O (as nitroxyl H2N2O2).
keyPoints: Needs alpha-H (primary or secondary nitro)
Tertiary nitroalkanes do not react
Nitro group acts as a masked carbonyl (umpolung)

examples.eq: CH3CH=NO2- Na+ + H2SO4 (aq) -> CH3CHO + N2O + Na2SO4 + H2O

jeeTips: Contrast with nitroalkane reduction (gives amines). Tertiary nitro: no alpha-H, no Nef. Nitroalkane tautomerism (nitro/aci) underpins.

name: Henry Reaction
summary: A nitroalkane with alpha-H adds to an aldehyde or ketone in base to give a beta-nitro alcohol, the nitro analogue of the aldol reaction.
mechanism: Base deprotonates the acidic alpha-H to give a nitronate carbanion, which attacks the carbonyl carbon; protonation gives the beta-nitro alcohol.
keyPoints: Nitro-stabilised carbanion (pKa about 10) is the nucleophile
Dehydration gives nitroalkene (C6H5CH=CHNO2)
Products can be reduced to beta-amino alcohols or converted by Nef to carbonyls
jeeTips: Aldol analogue with nitro carbanion. Compare Knoevenagel, aldol. The nitro compound supplies the nucleophile.

name: Robinson Annulation
summary: A ketone enolate undergoes Michael addition to methyl vinyl ketone, then an intramolecular aldol condensation closes a new six-membered ring to give a cyclohexenone fused to the starting ring.
mechanism: Enolate adds 1,4 to the enone (Michael). The resulting 1,5-diketone's methyl ketone enolises and attacks the other carbonyl (intramolecular aldol); dehydration gives the conjugated enone.
keyPoints: Michael addition followed by intramolecular aldol condensation
Forms a six-membered ring (annulation)
Steroid and terpenoid ring construction
jeeTips: Two steps: Michael then aldol (Michael + intramolecular aldol). Ring formed has six members.
